Stop. Before you call your car an asset, see which of these 4 things actually pays you.
An asset puts money in your pocket. A liability takes it out.
Max's coupe loses about half its value in five years, and still takes a payment every month. Liability.
Theo's index fund. Over the long run, the stock market has grown about 7 percent a year after inflation. Asset.
Max's side hustle: he buys sneakers and resells them for more than he paid. Asset. Max wins this one.
Their houses? It depends. A home you live in costs money every month. It only pays you when it earns more than it costs.
So before you buy something, ask one question: does it put money in your pocket, or take it out?
